scope: Native max_2 first-operand tie behavior, using the current bounded runtime ordering profile; not general Erlang term ordering or whole-file admission.
adaptations: Use the existing charged ordering helper: exact-equal terms, integers, floats, exactly representable mixed numeric operands, atoms and distinct admitted term ranks. Other comparisons terminate with explicit runtime-profile refusal, not a guest notsup exception or false guard.
Return the first operand on arithmetic equality, retaining integer versus float representation. No process-heap allocation or moving collection occurs.

Positively link max/2 as a non-GC BIF. Native body/guard dispatch preserves scratch OOM, accounted memory denial, invocation-work exhaustion and unsupported-profile outcomes before any guest failure branch. Schedule-out occurs only after the successor and result are published.

Compiler-produced fixtures and an independent OTP oracle cover integer/atom/rank ordering and mixed numeric ties. Runtime tests cover body/guard refusals, every work-credit prefix through exact completion, fallible scratch allocation and final accounted balance. These do not establish whole-application acceptance.
